note: Research for the lives view's real figures (Docs/hills-design/MODALITIES.md 7.3), read on 2026-11-03. Forbes net worth: for each candidate, every entry on Forbes's World's Billionaires list (spring) and Forbes 400 (fall) from 2005 to 2026, read from forbes.com's own list data: the JSON feed forbes.com's list pages load (forbesapi), one per list and year, queried for the fields named in the URL. Each value is the entry's finalWorth (US$ millions) / 1000, in billions of US dollars; its quote is the entry's text copied verbatim from that response (copied by script so it stays exact), and entryDate is the UTC date of the entry's own date field (not the list's date, which build.py computes). Every build re-verifies each quote, value, rank, month and entry date against the cached copy of the feed (Tools/lives/.cache; a value's verifiedOn in visibility.json is the day that copy was fetched): python3 -I Tools/lives/build.py --refresh re-downloads the 2026 feeds first, and deleting the cache re-fetches everything. Forbes's own revisions: build.py compares the candidates' values with archived copies of Forbes's list data in the Wayback Machine (revisionCheck below); an archived value that differs is kept as a separate value marked archived. Page views, Wikidata titles and the follower snapshot are fetched or copied by build.py and are not repeated here. No Instagram-only follower list (such as Wikipedia's list of the most-followed Instagram accounts) is used: the only follower figure is people.json's four-platform 2025 snapshot.

measures.pageViews: views a month of the person's English Wikipedia article (Wikimedia, all access, user agent), from July 2015

together.rule: the highest share of years in which log net worth and log page views moved the same way (both rose or both fell), year on year over 2016-2025: net worth is the World's Billionaires estimate of each year (every candidate is on that list every year) and page views are the calendar year's, so there are nine year-on-year moves; a year in which either series did not move is a year they did not move the same way, and it stays among the years counted (the caption reads 'together in k of 9 years'); at least 8 annual points; ties: more years, then the id

apart.rule: the lowest share, counted the same way; ties: more years, then the id

littleAttention.rule: the richest Forbes-400 American not among the most-followed accounts, with the fewest page views: among the candidates on the Forbes 400 of 2025 that the earlier rules did not pick, those outside the attention cloud (fewer than 10 million followers in the 2025 snapshot, the cloud of MODALITIES.md 5.2), the richest (ties: the fewer page views in 2025)
littleAttention.fallbackRule: if every such candidate is in the attention cloud, the rule picks nobody: the candidate with the fewest page views in 2025 (ties: the richer) is written as a proposal, not as the pick, and becomes the pick only when the author approves the shortlist naming it for littleAttention
littleAttention.basis: no candidate on the Forbes 400 2025 is outside the attention cloud (10M followers or more: all 5), so the rule picks nobody; fallback proposal: the fewest page views in 2025 among the candidates the earlier rules did not pick; the author left this rule without a pick

rules.distinct: each rule picks among the candidates the earlier rules did not pick (order: together, apart, little attention); the author's pick, when approved, is none of the rules' picks

picks.basis: no candidate on the Forbes 400 2025 is outside the attention cloud (10M followers or more: all 5), so the rule picks nobody; fallback proposal: the fewest page views in 2025 among the candidates the earlier rules did not pick; the author left this rule without a pick

picks.name: Oprah Winfrey
picks.caption: fortune held steady ($2.5B to $3.0B) while readership fell to 0.63 of 2016; together in 2 of 9 years
picks.basis: The author's third life, approved 3 Nov 2026 in place of the little-attention rule, which picks nobody inside people.json: Oprah Winfrey, shown with her own computed pattern, not as a rule's pick.

shortlist.note: The author approves the picks (MODALITIES.md 7.3). Until then the builder writes the computed picks with authorApproved false. To approve, set author_approved to true and approved to {"together": id, "apart": id, "littleAttention": id or null, "authorPick": id (optional)}; the build then fails if the rules ever pick someone else. When no candidate meets the little-attention condition, naming the fallback proposal's id for littleAttention accepts it as the pick, and null leaves that rule without a pick. authorPick names a third candidate the author chose, written with its own caption and never as a rule's pick.

forbesLists.note: listDate: the most common UTC date of the list's entries in today's list data (entries: rows on the list; onListDate: rows with that date). Before 2013 it is the first day of the list's month for most entries, so it marks the month rather than a day of publication or of measurement; an entry's own date is its entryDate

forbesRevisions.method: Forbes's own revisions are looked for by build.py, from the Wayback Machine. It reads the archive's index of captures (the queries below, status 200 only) at both addresses forbes.com has served its list data from: the older www.forbes.com/ajax/list/data?year=<year>&uri=<list>&type=person and the newer www.forbes.com/forbesapi/person/<list>/<year>/... It then compares every candidate's value, and rank where the copy keeps the list's rank, with today's list data: in every archived copy at the older address, and in the earliest and the latest readable copy at the newer address that holds the list in rank order from its first row (no country, industry or name filter, no search; a copy of the first page counts, and candidates beyond it are reported). A copy made within nearListDays of the list's date shows the values as first published, or nearly; a later copy shows them as of the day it was made, so it can reveal only a revision made after that day. Revisit records (a later capture identical to an earlier one) are not listed by the index queries. forbes.com's HTML list pages, which held the lists before the list data existed, were not searched. Read 2026-11-03.

pageViews.source: Wikimedia REST API, pageviews per article: en.wikipedia, all-access, user agent, monthly
pageViews.field: items[].views (one per month; a month the source has no row for is null)
pageViews.note: views of the article under its current title; views that arrive through redirects are counted by the source under the redirect's own title and are not included

annual.computed: netWorth: The World's Billionaires estimate of each year (billion US dollars); pageViews: the calendar year's monthly views summed; indices: each over its 2016 value; moves: the signs of the year-on-year change of log net worth and log page views ('=' unchanged: such a year counts as one in which they did not move the same way)
